solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Congratulatory gesture one way to make friends?

blocks.note: first meaning: a hearty pat between the shoulders to say well done
second, cryptic meaning: a word meaning smack, read the other way, spells a word for chums

explanation.walkthrough: BACK SLAP read literally: SLAP written back to front is PALS, so it is one way to make friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapping someone between the shoulder blades is a familiar gesture of congratulation.

clue.text: Risqué word that raises a smile: Danish?

definitions.note: an example of the answer, hence the question mark

blocks.note: a blue joke is a risqué one
what a photographer asks you to say to make you smile

explanation.surface: A cheeky word that makes a Dane grin.
explanation.walkthrough: Danish looks like a nationality or a pastry; it is Danish Blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish Blue is a well-known veined cheese from Denmark, an example of the type.

clue.text: Fur left behind by old pet

indicators.note: what is left behind once something departs is the rest, so a letter goes

blocks.note: an animal's fur is its coat
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Shed fur left on the sofa by an elderly family pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat is one of the commonest domestic animals kept as a companion.

clue.text: Exams set mostly especially for certain types of school?

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; the definition describes what it is used for

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is lost
set as in set in a new arrangement, telling us to reorder the letters

blocks.note: taken as written
set with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: Exam papers written with particular kinds of school in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Set does double duty here: it is shortened as fodder and also signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Single-sex schools for boys only or girls only are described as same-sex schools.

clue.text: Old defence area not fiddled with in high-scoring draw?

indicators.note: something fiddled has been tampered with, so these letters are shuffled
in places the abbreviated preceding word inside the score that follows

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
the letters to be rearranged
W is the standard abbreviation for with
a nine-all scoreline is a draw with lots of goals

explanation.surface: An old area of defence nobody has touched, in a goal-fest of a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiddled with reads as one phrase meaning tampered with, but with is split off as its own piece. The Romans built it after Hadrian's.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antonine Wall was a Roman fortification across central Scotland, the empire's northernmost frontier barrier.

clue.text: Agent runs after rent?

indicators.note: after tells us the runs letter is placed behind the word for rent

blocks.note: rent as the past participle of rend: torn apart, broken
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An estate agent chasing tenants who are behind with their rent.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent looks like money paid to a landlord; here it means torn.
explanation.definitionFit: A broker is someone who acts as an intermediary arranging deals for clients, an agent.

clue.text: Shock after submarine finds preserved fish

indicators.note: after says the word for shock is placed behind the other piece

blocks.note: a submarine, or sub, is a long sandwich roll
a shock of hair is a mop

explanation.surface: A navy vessel's crew get a nasty surprise when they discover some pickled fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Submarine is not a vessel but a sandwich, and shock is not surprise but hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a pickled herring fillet rolled around a filling, a kind of cured fish.

clue.text: High Mass having a major link with Islam originally, surprisingly

indicators.note: originally points to the origin, the first letter of the word before it
surprisingly says the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of Islam

explanation.surface: A church service with a surprising connection to Islam.
explanation.walkthrough: High Mass looks like a church service; it is a high mass of rock. With is a link joining the I to the rest of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is Africa's tallest mountain, a huge elevated landmass.

clue.text: Quietly finishing off drink, or what’s left?

indicators.note: finishing off means coming at the finish, after everything else

blocks.note: rum is a spirit
P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone quietly draining a glass, or what remains in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rump is a remnant, the small leftover part of something larger, as in a rump parliament.

clue.text: Extremely useful bird boxes at last!

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, the two end letters of the next word
to box something is to enclose it, so one word sits inside another

blocks.note: the first and last letters of useful
bird is slang for a prison sentence, as in doing bird
taken as written

explanation.surface: An enthusiast's delight at a very handy nesting box for birds, finally found.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird for a prison term comes from rhyming slang, birdlime = time. Last is the definition, not an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimate means final or coming at the very end, which is what last means.

clue.text: Navigation with Poles winding down

blocks.note: surface reading: a voyage with Polish sailors on a meandering course
setter's reading: steering between poles while zigzagging down a ski slope

explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes Poles look like people from Poland; they are the gate poles of a ski course.
explanation.definitionFit: This ski race requires the skier to weave a winding route downhill between pairs of flagged poles.

clue.text: Legendary weapons in truth cleaned out: fails to secure enough?

indicators.note: cleaned out means emptied, so only the outside letters stay

blocks.note: the first and last letters of truth
read as under-bolts: bolts too little, so does not lock things up well enough

explanation.surface: A myth about weapons that fail when truth is purged and security is lax.
explanation.walkthrough: UNDER BOLTS is a made-up verb phrase, to bolt insufficiently.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunderbolts are the mythical missiles hurled by gods such as Zeus and Thor.

clue.text: Line’s included in church hymn: we must think it’s a bloomer!

indicators.note: included in says one piece goes inside the pair of words that follow

blocks.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
RY, railway, is a line; the possessive adds S
an anthem is a choral hymn
um is the noise we make while we stop to think

explanation.surface: A churchgoer struggles over a line of a hymn and declares the result a howler.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is British slang for a blunder, which suits the surface; here it means something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A chrysanthemum is a flowering garden plant, so it is literally something that blooms.

clue.text: Blame screen for distorting likeness

indicators.note: distorting twists things out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Blame the screen for a distorted picture of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Resemblance and likeness are synonyms for similarity in appearance between two things.

clue.text: Article by a couple of boys eclipses what one puts in the paper

definitions.text: what one puts in the paper

indicators.note: to eclipse is to hide something behind, here by wrapping round it

blocks.note: per means by, as in per annum
two words for a boy, son and lad
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece written by two lads overshadows readers' own contributions.
explanation.walkthrough: Article and paper suggest journalism, but the article is just the little word a.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal ad is a short notice placed in a newspaper's classified columns, often seeking a partner.

clue.text: Times goes on being a favourite of the Queen

indicators.note: goes on means the multiplication sign is added onto the end of the word for being

blocks.note: esse is Latin for to be, used in philosophy for existence
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A newspaper keeps going on about being one of the monarch's favourites.
explanation.walkthrough: Times is not the newspaper but the multiplication sign. The Queen is Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Devereux, Earl of Essex, was a famous courtier and favourite of Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Gripping new English writer is pleasant change

indicators.note: something gripping another holds it fast inside itself

blocks.note: nice is a mild synonym for pleasant
N is the abbreviation for new
E is the abbreviation for English
a pen is the classic crossword writer

explanation.surface: A gripping new English author makes a nice change.
explanation.walkthrough: NICE holds N, E and PEN: NI(NEPEN)CE. Ninepence was an amount in old British pre-decimal money.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninepence is a small sum of money, the sort of loose coins you get back as change.

clue.text: Military band ridiculously bars women

indicators.note: ridiculously suggests the following letters are rearranged in an absurd way

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An army marching band absurdly excludes female musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: Band here is a strap, not musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sam Browne is an officer's belt with a supporting strap over the shoulder, worn in military uniform.

clue.text: Strip of green clothing transformed the design afresh

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so these letters change order
clothing means dressing round, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: in bowls a rink is one strip of the bowling green
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A green fabric strip in the clothing changes the outfit's design.
explanation.walkthrough: Green and clothing suggest fashion; green is a bowling green, the lawn on which the game of bowls is played.
explanation.definitionFit: To rethink something is to consider it again and plan it anew, so to redesign it.

clue.text: Gather confession from fool

blocks.note: first meaning: collect together, accumulate
second, cryptic meaning: what a fool admits, (I) am (an) ass

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as AM ASS and it becomes a fool's admission of foolishness.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate a large quantity of something, which is to gather it.

clue.text: Country tune, say: part of it almost certainly recalled

indicators.note: recalled as in called back, so the whole string runs backwards

blocks.note: an air is a tune
e.g., for example, is what say means here
la is a sol-fa note, and almost any tune will contain it

explanation.surface: A country-and-western song, part of which you are almost sure to remember.
explanation.walkthrough: AIR EG LA reversed. Country and tune together suggest country music, but country is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a large North African nation whose capital is Algiers.

clue.text: Magnitude of blow dealt by defeat here indeterminate?

definitions.note: names the place of a famous defeat

blocks.note: a size left indeterminate, small and large at once
a horn is something you blow

explanation.surface: Historians cannot agree how hard a blow a famous defeat dealt.
explanation.walkthrough: Indeterminate tells you the magnitude is both little and big. Blow looks like a punch; read it as the verb, and a horn is what is blown.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of the Little Bighorn in Montana was the 1876 rout of Custer's Seventh Cavalry.

clue.text: It follows forthwith — usually — but not all of it

indicators.note: not all of it means just a portion of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Something follows immediately, as a rule, though only in part.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus introduces a consequence: it follows that, or therefore, in logical argument.

clue.text: What you keep with practice or give up?

blocks.note: first meaning: from the idiom keep your ... , to stay in practice
second meaning: to submit or surrender, as homework or a resignation

explanation.definitionFit: You keep your hand in by regular practice, and to hand in work is to submit or surrender it.

clue.text: Such errors often attributed to ministers?

definitions.text: Such errors often attributed to ministers?

blocks.clueFragment: Such errors often attributed to ministers?
blocks.note: surface reading: government ministers blaming mistakes on civil servants' typing

blocks.clueFragment: Such errors often attributed to ministers?
blocks.note: setter's reading: ministers as clergy, so their errors are those of the clergy

explanation.walkthrough: Ministers look like politicians; read them as clergymen and the office slip becomes a churchly one.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerical error is an office slip, and clerical also means relating to the clergy.

clue.text: Largely hair-raising mountain route?

indicators.note: largely means for the most part, so the last letter is dropped
in a down entry raising means lifting the letters so they read upwards

blocks.note: a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: A frightening pass through the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: Hair-raising looks like one word meaning terrifying; it splits into hair and raising.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is a low pass between two peaks, a route across a mountain ridge.

clue.text: Viewing aid picked up the smallest things

indicators.note: picked up as in heard on a radio, so we want a sound not a spelling

blocks.note: specs are spectacles, an aid to seeing

explanation.surface: Glasses that let you see the tiniest details.
explanation.definitionFit: Specks are tiny particles or spots, the smallest things you could see.

clue.text: A second girl’s turned set on

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the girl's name is read from right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second
Delia is a girl's name; the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: A girl turns up a second time and pounces on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: DELIAS read backwards is SAILED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be set on is to be attacked, and assailed means violently attacked.
